_comment: The WHERE clauses the legacy Forms blocks apply to every query of the block, for the
blocks whose clause $filter cannot express. A request names one: ?where=AT5521.OUTSHIPMT.
The text never comes from the client.
Reviewed and placed by hand, like relationships.json. Nothing writes this at runtime.
name       form.BLOCK, as the request names it. Unique.
entitySet  the table the block queries. The name is valid against this table only.
sql        the predicate as the form wrote it. No semicolon, no comment, balanced parens.
binds      values the screen supplies. Write :NAME in the sql with dots turned to
underscores, so the Forms name MATL.CNTNR_SEQ_ID is :MATL_CNTNR_SEQ_ID in the
sql and arrives as bind.MATL.CNTNR_SEQ_ID on the request. type is number,
string or date. A declared bind missing from the sql, or a bind used in the
sql but not declared, is rejected at startup and logged as an error.
note      where it came from and anything a reviewer should know.
Seeded with the three clauses API-HANDOFF-Block-Where.md quotes in full. The rest of the
twenty are abridged in that document and are to arrive generated from the forms.

blockWheres.name: AT5510.OUTSHIPMT
blockWheres.sql: SHIPMENT_NBR IN (SELECT SHIPMENT_NBR FROM AT_SHIPMENTS WHERE SUBSTR(SHIPMENT_TYPE_CD,1,8) <> 'TRANSFER')
blockWheres.note: AT5510 block OUTSHIPMT. Excludes transfer shipments. Quoted in full in API-HANDOFF-Block-Where.md, 30 Sep 2026.

blockWheres.name: AT5511.OUTSHIPMT
blockWheres.sql: SHIPMENT_NBR IN (SELECT SHIPMENT_NBR FROM AT_SHIPMENTS WHERE SUBSTR(SHIPMENT_TYPE_CD,1,8) <> 'TRANSFER')
blockWheres.note: AT5511 block OUTSHIPMT. Same clause as AT5510; kept as its own name so either screen can change without touching the other.

blockWheres.name: AT5521.OUTSHIPMT
blockWheres.sql: DISP_SITE_SEQ_ID = 2 AND SHIPMENT_NBR IN (SELECT SHIPMENT_NBR FROM AT_SHIPMENTS WHERE SHIPMENT_DT IS NOT NULL)
blockWheres.note: AT5521 block OUTSHIPMT. The subquery is over 62,719 rows, which is why a two-step IN list will not fit a URL.
